subject: math
title: Numbers to 20: Count, Ten Frames, Compare
seo_title: Grade 1 Math Numbers to 20 Worksheets: Ten Frames, Free with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on numbers to 20 for the BC curriculum: count objects, ten frames, teen numbers as 10 and some more, compare and order with more and fewer, and number lines and word problems. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Every teen number is 10 and some more: 14 = 10 + 4.
key_sub: Write the 1 ten first: 1 ten and 2 ones is 12, not 21. Touch each thing once when you count, so nothing is counted twice.
body_html:
Count each thing once

Touch each thing as you count it. Count each thing only once. Groups of 5 and 10 make counting fast.

Ten frames

A ten frame has 10 boxes. A full ten frame is 10. The empty boxes tell you how many more make 10. For numbers past 10, use two ten frames.

10 and some more

Every number from 11 to 19 is 10 and some more. A rod is 10. A small cube is 1.

10 and some more

17 = 10 + ☐

17 is 1 ten and 7 ones. The ten is 10. The ones are 7.

Answer: 7

Read and write number words

NumberWordNumberWord
11eleven16sixteen
12twelve17seventeen
13thirteen18eighteen
14fourteen19nineteen
15fifteen20twenty

In “fourteen” you hear the 4 first. But you write the 1 first: 14.

Compare: more and fewer

Count both groups. Do not look at how long a row is. To compare numbers, look at the tens first, then the ones.

Which is greater?

Which is greater, 15 or 12?

Both have 1 ten. 5 ones is more than 2 ones.

Answer: 15

Number lines

On a number line, numbers get bigger to the right. Find a number you know. Then count the marks.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 21 for 12Write the 1 ten first: 1 ten and 2 ones is 12
Counting one thing twiceTouch each thing once, or cross it off
Counting the empty boxes in a ten frameCount the counters. Empty boxes show how many more make 10
Reading the rod as 1 (1 rod and 4 cubes = 5)A rod is 10: 10, then 11, 12, 13, 14
Writing 110 after 19After 19 comes a new ten: 20
Thinking a longer row has moreCount both rows. Spread-out things can be fewer

faq.q: What numbers should a Grade 1 student know in BC?
faq.a: In the BC curriculum, Grade 1 students learn number concepts to 20. They count, read, write and show numbers to 20, see teen numbers as 10 and some more, and compare and order them.

faq.q: How do ten frames help Grade 1 students?
faq.a: A ten frame shows 10 in two rows of 5, so children see amounts at a glance and see how many more make 10. One full frame and 4 more is 14.

faq.q: Why does my child write 21 for 12?
faq.a: In words like “sixteen” you hear the 6 first, so children often write the digits in the wrong order. Build the number with 1 rod and some cubes and say “1 ten first, then the ones” while writing it.

faq.q: How can I practise numbers to 20 at home?
faq.a: Count real things together, like shells, pine cones or toys, and touch each one once. Put 10 in a group, then count on: 10, 11, 12.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: Touch each one once: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. There are 5 balls. 6 means one was counted twice.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: The first 5 make a group. Count on: 6, 7. Touch each one only once. There are 7 apples. 8 means one was counted twice. 2 counts only the ones after the group of 5.
The first 5 make a group. Count on: 6, 7, 8. Touch each one only once. There are 8 stars. 9 means one was counted twice. 3 counts only the ones after the group of 5.
There are 9 stars. 1 more than 9 is 10. Count on: 9, 10.
The first 5 make a group. Count on: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Touch each one only once. There are 10 buttons. 11 means one was counted twice. 5 counts only one group of 5.

items.q: How many pucks?
items.e: The full row has 10. Then count on: 11. There are 11 pucks. Do not write 2. The first row is 1 ten, not 1.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12. There are 12 balls. Write the 1 ten first: 12, not 21.

items.q: How do you say this number?
items.e: 13 is 1 ten and 3 ones. We say thirteen. Thirty is 30.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13. There are 13 apples. Write the 1 ten first: 13, not 31.
The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14. There are 14 stars. Write the 1 ten first: 14, not 41.
The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. There are 15 buttons. Write the 1 ten first: 15, not 51. 5 counts only the second row.

items.q: Leah eats 1 apple. How many apples are left?
items.e: There are 15 apples. 1 less than 15 is 14. Count back: 15, 14. 16 is 1 more, not 1 less.

items.q: How many pucks?
items.e: The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. There are 16 pucks. Write the 1 ten first: 16, not 61. 6 counts only the second row.

items.q: Which number is this?
items.e: Seventeen is 1 ten and 7 ones. Write 17. You hear “seven” first, but write the 1 first. Seventy is 70.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. There are 17 apples. Write the 1 ten first: 17, not 71. 7 counts only the second row.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18. There are 18 balls. Write the 1 ten first: 18, not 81.

items.q: Ava counts 13 balls. She counted one ball twice. How many balls are there?
items.e: Ava counted one ball two times, so 13 is 1 too many. Count again and touch each ball once: 10, then 11, 12. There are 12 balls.
The full row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. There are 19 stars. Write the 1 ten first: 19, not 91. 9 counts only the second row.

items.q: Count by 1s. What comes next?
items.e: After 19 comes a new ten: 20. Do not write 110.
Each full row has 10. Count the rows by tens: 10, 20. There are 20 buttons. 2 tens is 20, not 2.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: Count the counters, not the empty boxes. The top row has 4. There are 4 counters. 6 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: Count the counters, not the empty boxes. The top row has 5. Count on: 6. There are 6 counters. 4 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes: there are 5. 5 and 5 make 10. 10 is the whole frame, not the missing part.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: Count the counters, not the empty boxes. The top row has 5. Count on: 6, 7, 8. There are 8 counters. 2 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes: there are 3. 7 and 3 make 10. 7 is how many counters there are now.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: Every box has a counter. A full ten frame is 10. It is 1 ten, but the number is 10, not 1.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes: there is 1. 9 and 1 make 10. 9 is how many counters there are now. 10 is the whole frame, not the missing part.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes: there are 8. 2 and 8 make 10. 2 is how many counters there are now.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: The full ten frame is 10. Then count on: 11. There are 11 counters. 9 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: The full ten frame is 10. Then count on: 11, 12. There are 12 counters. Write the tens first: 12, not 21.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: The full ten frame is 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13. There are 13 counters. 7 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: The full ten frame is 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14. There are 14 counters. 4 counts only the second frame.

items.q: How many more counters make 20?
items.e: The first frame is full. The second frame has 5 counters and 5 empty boxes. 15 and 5 make 20. 15 is how many counters there are now.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: The full ten frame is 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. There are 16 counters. Write the tens first: 16, not 61.

items.q: How many more counters make 20?
items.e: The first frame is full. The second frame has 8 counters and 2 empty boxes. 18 and 2 make 20. 18 is how many counters there are now.

items.q: What number do the ten frames show?
items.e: The full ten frame is 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. There are 17 counters. 18 means one counter was counted twice.

items.q: How many more counters make 20?
items.e: The first frame is full. The second frame has 3 counters and 7 empty boxes. 13 and 7 make 20. 13 is how many counters there are now.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: The full ten frame is 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. There are 19 counters. 18 means one counter was missed.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: Both ten frames are full. Count by tens: 10, 20. There are 20 counters. 2 tens is 20, not 2.

items.q: How many more counters make 20?
items.e: The first frame is full. The second frame has 1 counter and 9 empty boxes. 11 and 9 make 20. 11 is how many counters there are now.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: The rod is 10. Then count on the cubes: 11, 12, 13. 1 ten and 3 ones is 13. Write the ten first: 13, not 31 or 103.

items.q: How many tens are in 19?
items.e: There is 1 rod. A rod is 1 ten. 19 has 1 ten and 9 ones.

items.q: How many ones are in 16?
items.e: Count the small cubes: 6. 16 has 1 ten and 6 ones.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: The rod is 10. Then count on the cubes: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. 1 ten and 6 ones is 16. 7 counts the rod as 1, not 10.

items.q: 10 + 2 = ☐
items.e: 1 bundle is 10 sticks. 2 more sticks: 11, 12. So 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Which number is 1 ten and 1 one?
items.e: 1 ten is 10. 1 more one makes 11. Use only 2 digits, not 101.

items.q: 14 = 10 + ☐
items.e: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. The rod is 10. The cubes are 4. So 14 = 10 + 4.

items.q: 10 + 5 = ☐
items.e: One full frame is 10. 5 more counters: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. So 10 + 5 = 15. 6 adds 1 and 5, but the full frame is 10.

items.q: Which matches the ten frames?
items.e: 1 frame is full: 1 ten. The other frame has 2 counters: 2 ones. That is 1 ten and 2 ones. 8 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: Which number has 1 ten and 0 ones?
items.e: 1 ten is 10 cubes in a rod. There are no loose cubes, so write 0 ones: 10.

items.q: 17 = 10 + ☐
items.e: The full frame is 10. The other frame has 7 counters. So 17 = 10 + 7. 3 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: 1 bundle of 10 sticks and 8 more. How many sticks?
items.e: The bundle is 10. Count on 8: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18. There are 18 sticks.

items.q: 10 + ☐ = 11
items.e: 11 is 1 ten and 1 one. 10 and 1 more make 11.

items.q: ☐ + 9 = 19
items.e: 19 is 1 ten and 9 ones. The rod is 10, not 1. So 10 + 9 = 19.

items.q: Which is the same as 13?
items.e: 13 is 1 ten and 3 ones. 1 ten is 10. So 13 = 10 + 3. 1 + 3 is only 4.

items.q: Put 10 cubes together to make a rod. How many cubes are left?
items.e: 15 is 10 and 5 more. 10 cubes make the rod. 5 cubes are left. So 15 is 1 ten and 5 ones.

items.q: Take away the rod. How many are left? 17 − 10 = ☐
items.e: 17 is 10 and 7 more. Take away the 10. 7 are left. 16 takes away only 1.
Both frames are full. Each frame is 10. So 20 = 10 + 10.

items.q: 10 + 10 = ☐
items.e: Each bundle is 10. Count by tens: 10, 20. So 10 + 10 = 20.

items.q: Add 1 more cube. What number is it now?
items.e: The blocks show 19. 1 more cube makes 10 cubes. 10 cubes make 1 more ten. Now there are 2 tens: 20. Do not write 110.

sets.title: Compare and order: more and fewer

items.q: Which row has more apples?
items.e: Count each row. Row A has 7. Row B has 9. 9 is more than 7, so Row B has more. Row A is longer, but its apples are far apart.

items.q: Which row has fewer balls?
items.e: Count each row. Row A has 4. Row B has 6. 4 is less than 6, so Row A has fewer. Do not look at how long the row is.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All the numbers have 1 ten. Look at the ones: 9 is the most. 19 is the greatest.
Row A has 8. Row B has 8. They are the same. Row B only looks longer.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 20 has 2 tens, so it is not the least. 17, 12 and 15 have 1 ten. Look at the ones: 2 is the fewest. 12 is the least.

items.q: How many more balls are in Row B?
items.e: Match each ball in Row A with one in Row B. 3 balls in Row B have no match. Row B has 3 more. 9 is all of Row B, and 15 adds the rows.

items.q: Which number is less than 10?
items.e: 8 has no tens. 10, 11 and 12 have 1 ten. So 8 is less than 10.

items.q: Which blocks show the greater number?
items.e: A is 9 cubes: 9. B is 1 rod and 1 cube: 11. 11 is more than 9, so B is greater. A has more pieces, but the rod is 10.
Row A has 11. Row B has 9. 9 is less than 11, so Row B has fewer. Row B is longer, but its buttons are far apart.

items.q: Which number is greater than 15?
items.e: 18 comes after 15 when you count. So 18 is greater than 15. 15 is equal to 15, not greater.

items.q: How many fewer apples are in Row B?
items.e: Row A has 10. Row B has 7. 7 and 3 make 10, so Row B has 3 fewer.

items.q: Which blocks show the smaller number?
items.e: Both have 1 ten. A has 4 ones and B has 7 ones. 14 is less than 17, so A is smaller.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: On a number line, numbers get bigger to the right. 13 is to the left of 16. So 13 is less than 16.

items.q: Which number is 1 less than 16?
items.e: 1 less means count back 1: 16, 15. 17 is 1 more. 6 is 10 less.

items.q: Which blocks show the greater number?
items.e: Both have 1 ten. Look at the ones: A has 8 and B has 5. 18 is more than 15, so A is greater.

items.q: Put the numbers in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 8 has no tens, so it is the least. 12 and 15 have 1 ten. 2 ones is less than 5 ones. The order is 8, 12, 15.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 20 has 2 tens. 10 and 12 have 1 ten. 2 has no tens. 20 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is between 14 and 17?
items.e: Between 14 and 17 come 15 and 16. 16 is one of them. 17 is the end, not between.

items.q: Put the numbers in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 20 has 2 tens, so it comes first. 17 has more ones than 11. The order is 20, 17, 11.

items.q: Put the numbers in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 1 and 9 have no tens, and 1 is less than 9. 10 and 19 have 1 ten, and 10 has fewer ones. The order is 1, 9, 10, 19.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. Count from 5: 6, 7, 8. The arrow points to 8.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. Count from 10: 11, 12, 13. The arrow points to 13.

items.q: Which letter shows 16?
items.e: Find 15. Count on 1 mark: 16. The letter is C. B is 14, which is 1 mark before 15.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. Count from 15: 16, 17. The arrow points to 17.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. It is 1 before 20. The arrow points to 19.

items.q: The arrow is at 12. Jump 3 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Jump right 1 mark at a time: 13, 14, 15. Do not count 12 as a jump. 9 is 3 to the left.

items.q: Lucas sees 9 bald eagles. Then 1 more lands. How many now?
items.e: 1 more than 9 is 10. Now the ten frame is full.
1 more than 12 is 13. Count on 1: 12, 13. 11 is 1 less.

items.q: Liam puts hockey pucks in rows of 10. How many pucks?
items.e: 1 full row is 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. There are 16 pucks.

items.q: Sofia has 1 bundle of 10 sticks and 4 more. How many sticks?
items.e: The bundle is 10. Count on: 11, 12, 13, 14. She has 14 sticks.

items.q: Nadia needs 20 pine cones for art. She has 18. How many more?
items.e: There are 2 empty boxes. 18 and 2 make 20.

items.q: Yesterday was day 19 of school. What day is today?
items.e: Today is 1 day after 19. After 19 comes 20.

items.q: Owen wears this hockey jersey. How many tens are in his number?
items.e: The number is 17. The 1 is in the tens place. 17 has 1 ten and 7 ones.

items.q: Hana’s class is in Room 12. Which digit is in the ones place?
items.e: 12 is 1 ten and 2 ones. The ones digit is the last digit: 2.

items.q: Zara finds 15 shells. Owen finds 12 shells. Who has more?
items.e: Both have 1 ten. Look at the ones: 5 is more than 2. Zara has more.

items.q: Mei reads 17 books. Wei reads 19 books. Who reads fewer?
items.e: 17 comes before 19 when you count. 17 is less, so Mei reads fewer.

items.q: A BC Ferries boat has 10 cars on one deck. It has 5 cars on the other deck. How many cars?
items.e: 10 and 5 more is 1 ten and 5 ones. 10 + 5 = 15 cars.

items.q: Arjun counts 16 apples. He counted one apple twice. How many apples are there?
items.e: 16 is 1 too many, because one apple was counted twice. Touch each apple once: 10, then 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. There are 15 apples.

items.q: My number is between 10 and 20. It has 6 ones. What is it?
items.e: Between 10 and 20 means 1 ten. 1 ten and 6 ones is 16.

items.q: Four friends count rocks at the beach. Who has the most?
items.e: All the numbers have 1 ten. Look at the ones: 8 is the most. Mei has 18.
